issues.desc: What may be said and how products must be packaged and labelled.

gaps.why: The act that added the three twenty-mile rules and created the Ombudsman was the one cannabis act whose enacted text was not held locally, so its sections were recorded from the bill status page and the statutory matrix instead of parsed.
gaps.rec: Fetch the enacted PDF from the CGA public acts path.
gaps.st: CLOSED — the enacted PDF was fetched from the CGA public acts path and parsed. P.A. 23-79 now contributes 52 sections to the change record, including the section that put the twenty-mile rule into 21a-420j(e).

gaps.what: Committee agendas and meeting minutes, 2021 to 2026
gaps.why: Needed to establish when a provision was taken up and by whom, and to date the point at which language entered a substitute.
gaps.rec: Committee agendas; meeting minutes; the vote tally sheets behind each joint favorable report.

gaps.why: The bill status pages give LCO numbers but not who requested each amendment. Authorship of language is therefore unknown for most amendments in this dataset.
gaps.rec: LCO drafting request records where not exempt from disclosure.

gaps.why: The eLicense register carries no field linking a backer to the establishment backed, so every cap and affiliate test in the statute is unverifiable from public data.
gaps.rec: The backer disclosure schedules filed with each licence application.

gaps.why: These contain the organizing documents CGS 21a-420u(c) requires, naming each backer’s ownership stake, initial investment and payout terms. Without them the fifty per cent ownership limb cannot be tested for any venture.
gaps.rec: Approval packets and Council minutes for every venture, including rescinded approvals.

gaps.what: Any record construing the repealed twenty-mile rules for the period they were in force
gaps.why: Former CGS 21a-420u(f), 21a-420j(e) and 21a-420m(f) were repealed effective 1 January 2026. Whether the Department ever treated them as engaged, and how it measured distance, is not in any published record.
gaps.rec: Guidance, declaratory rulings under CGS 4-176, enforcement actions and internal memoranda for 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2025, and any savings clause construction.

gaps.why: No published file states which hybrid retailer licence converted from which dispensary facility licence. Every conversion in the ownership package is reconstructed rather than read, and for twenty active hybrid retailers even reconstruction fails.
gaps.rec: Conversion applications and approvals under CGS 21a-420t.

gaps.what: Lottery AWARDS, as distinct from entries
gaps.why: The published applicant list records entries bought, not awards made. For every company that entered both lotteries the award route is unresolvable.
gaps.rec: Lottery award records naming the winning applicant for each licence.

gaps.what: The Policies and Procedures document history for the adult-use market
gaps.why: Adult-use requirements sit in a policy document rather than adopted regulations. The version history and the authority relied on for each change are not published.
gaps.rec: Every version of the Policies and Procedures with adoption dates and the authority cited.

gaps.what: Written testimony recorded as NOT RETRIEVED
gaps.why: 67 of the 683 testimony records in this dataset had not been retrieved. They were listed rather than omitted, which is what made it possible to go back and get them.
gaps.st: CLOSED (66 of 67) — the files were reachable the whole time. The earlier failure was a URL-encoding fault on filenames containing spaces and commas, not a missing document. One file is still unreachable.

gaps.why: Registrations establish that a client sought to influence legislation. They do not say what was asked for, of whom, or when.
gaps.rec: Client issue reports at the bill level, where filed.

gaps.who: Department of Consumer Protection; Social Equity Council
gaps.why: The access log records public events. Who met whom privately, and when, is not published.
gaps.rec: Commissioner’s and Council members’ calendars and meeting records.
